1. General Information
1.1 Disclaimer
This Request to Participate information document (the “RTP”), the associated RTP response document
(“RTP Response Document”) issued separately by IDA Ireland as part of this procurement process for
the establishment of a framework agreement for the provision of the design, delivery and
management of IDA Ireland’s Property Management System (the “Procurement Process”) and any
clarification circulars issued by IDA Ireland (together the “Documents” and where the context allows,
a “Document”) are for information only and do not constitute, and shall not be interpreted as, an offer
for sale, prospectus, or the basis of a contract.
Candidates (as defined in section 3.1 of this RTP) are recommended to read the documents
thoroughly. While all reasonable steps have been taken to ensure that the information set out in the
Document is accurate and up to date, no representation or warranty, express or implied, is or will be
made or given in relation to the accuracy or the completeness of any information contained in the
Document or otherwise provided by or on behalf of IDA Ireland (in writing or otherwise) to any
interested party or its advisers. No responsibility or liability for any loss or damage arising as a result
of reliance on these documents, or for the information contained in these documents or for any
omission is or will be accepted by IDA Ireland or by any of its officers, employees, agents or
professional advisers. No officer, employee, agent, or professional adviser of the company has any
authority to give or make any representation or warranty, express or implied, in relation to such
information. IDA Ireland’s officers, employees, agents, and professional advisers expressly disclaim
any and all liability arising out of such documentation or information and any errors or omissions in or
from the documents and information.
IDA Ireland reserves the right, at any time and without notice or liability, not to proceed with some or
all of the Procurement Process, to terminate the Procurement Process (or any part thereof), to change
the basis of and the procedures for the bidding process and/or to procure the PMS by alternative means
if, in IDA Ireland’s opinion and at its sole discretion, it appears that it can be thereby more advantageously
procured.
1.2 Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Participation
It isthe policy of IDA Ireland to promote participation by Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises(“SMEs”)
on a fair and equal basis.
All firms are encouraged to explore the possibilities of forming relationships with SMEs or other
enterprises to meet the financial, economic or technical capacity requirements of the Procurement
Process and/or deliverables under the framework agreement/contracts, if required.
Candidates are reminded that they may rely on the resources of other entities to establish the
requirements on condition that they can prove to the satisfaction of IDA Ireland that they will have
these resources at their disposal when necessary – please see Section 5 of this RTP below.
Candidates may include individuals, partnerships, limited companies, groupings or any combination
of the foregoing with or without legal personality.5
If the response is from a Consortium (defined below), Candidates must ensure that all the relevant
information is provided and where necessary, provide the information requested separately for each
party. Relevant information relates to where a Candidate is relying on the resources to qualify (e.g.,
turnover, personnel, previous experience) and / or to deliver contracts. The Consortium must appoint
a single point of contact (a “Prime Contractor” as defined in section 5.5.5 of this RTP) who will assume
overall responsibility for delivery, and who is authorised to sign the Framework Agreement / contract
on behalf of all consortia members. IDA Ireland will not act as an arbitrator between members of a
Consortium.
Further details will be specified in the Invitation to Tender issued as part of this Procurement Process
to shortlisted Candidates.
1.3 Use of the RTP Response Document
IDA Ireland has provided the RTP Response Document as a separate document for Candidates to use
in preparing their response (Appendix A RTP Response Document). This document and format must
be used. Candidates should note that personalisation of the RTP Response Document is not allowed,
and they must not add their branding/colours to the RTP Response Document.
Please note that in addition to this RTP and the RTP Response Document, any clarification circulars
issued by IDA Ireland during the qualification submission period form part of the RTP Response
Document and this RTP. Candidates must ensure they regularly monitor eTenders and review any
clarifications published.
Please do not embed any web links in the documents submitted as they cannot be accessed. It is
recommended to upload your response in eTenders as a Zip file in order to protect the integrity of
file names.
1.4 Summary
Contracting Authority IDA Ireland

2. About IDA Ireland
IDA Ireland is the authority responsible for this procurement.
IDA Ireland is the State agency responsible for attracting and developing foreign direct investment into
Ireland. Its statutory mandate is set out in the Industrial Development Acts 1986–2019. IDA Ireland’s
main objective is to encourage investment into Ireland by foreign owned companies. It works as a
strategic partner and provides consultancy and support services free of charge to help organisations
set up and grow. Its success is measured by the impact of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and IDAsupported companies on the Irish economy.
IDA Ireland works closely with Government Departments, Enterprise Ireland, and other State
agencies as part of the broader enterprise ecosystem to deliver on Ireland’s economic development
objectives. IDA Ireland maintains a network of international offices and works with prospective
investors to identify suitable locations in Ireland. A core function of IDA Ireland involves the
management and development of its property portfolio, including the provision of sites and buildings
to support investment projects.
Further information on IDA Ireland’s functions and activities is available at
https://www.idaireland.com/
3. About the Framework Agreement and the Procurement Procedure
IDA Ireland proposes to engage in the Procurement Process for the establishment of a single-party
framework agreement for the provision of the design, delivery and management of IDA Ireland’s
Property Management System (PMS) the “Framework Agreement”.
The Property Management System (PMS) means the Salesforce based Property management
System to be designed, implemented, supported and enhanced under the Framework Agreement.
A framework agreement constitutes a means of establishing overall terms and conditions in
accordance with which, for a specified duration, individual contracts (known as “Call-Off Contracts”)
may (or may not) be awarded.
It is emphasised that the Framework Agreement constitutes no guarantee to purchase a specific
quantity of supplies or services from a particular economic operator. Indeed, IDA Ireland reserves the
right to operate outside of the Framework Agreement at its sole and absolute discretion, particularly
should it become apparent that doing so would offer greater value for money or if IDA Ireland requires
more specialist services. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Framework Agreement approach has
been adopted in order to leverage efficiencies and maximise cost savings over the duration of the
Framework Agreement.
IDA Ireland intends to award the initial Call-Off Contract from the Framework Agreement (the “Initial
Call-Off Contract”) to the first ranked tenderer as determined by the application of the award criteria
(the “Preferred Tenderer”) at the same time as the Framework Agreement. Under the Framework
Agreement, subsequent Call-Off Contracts may be awarded to the Preferred Tenderer at the discretion
of IDA Ireland. IDA Ireland shall not be obliged to award any particular number of subsequent Call-Off
Contracts or any particular value.IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 7
3.1 Purpose of the RTP Documentation
The purpose of the RTP documentation is to:
(i) provide interested persons with the information that they need to decide whether to
participate in this Procurement Process;
(ii) facilitate the submission of completed RTP Response Documents by interested persons (each
person who submits an RTP Response Document hereinafter being referred to as a
“Candidate”);
(iii) facilitate IDA Ireland in assessing the quality of the Candidates and their legal, financial and
technical capacities to meet the requirements of the Framework Agreement and Call-Off
Contracts; and
(iv) allow IDA Ireland to identify a number of suitably qualified and experienced Candidates who
will be invited to participate in the Tender Phase (as defined in section 3.7 of this RTP) of the
Procurement Process.
The information provided in this RTP will be supplemented during the Tender Phase of the
Procurement Process.
3.2 Numbers Admitted to the Framework Agreement
The Framework Agreement will be established as a single party framework agreement with the
Preferred Tenderer following the conclusion of the Procurement Process.
3.3 Duration
3.3.1 Duration of the Framework Agreement
The maximum duration of the Framework Agreement will be four (4) years with the option to extend
by up to three (3) years subject to satisfactory annual review of performance. For the avoidance of
doubt, IDA Ireland confirms that the period of any Call-off Contract awarded under the Framework
Agreement may extend beyond the date of expiry of the Framework Agreement.
While significant work has been undertaken on an initial discovery phase whereby user stories have been
developed, the successful supplier may be required to undertake potentially significant upfront time
investment in further discovery, detailed solution design, data migration, configuration, testing,
integration and organisational change activities. The option of the extension of the framework to a
maximum of 7 years will allow the IDA (provided that the successful supplier has performed in a
satisfactory manner) to obtain the benefit of the framework support as envisaged in the event of a
prolonged implementation period.
3.3.2 Duration of the Initial Call-Off Contract
It is anticipated that the Initial Call‑Off Contract will be awarded simultaneously with the Framework
Agreement. The duration of the Initial Call-Off Contract will be for a period of four (4) years with the IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 8
option to extend by up to three (3) years. This extension provision (if used) would be exercised in Year 4
of the Framework Agreement and allow the potential additional three (3) years to be applied flexibly, for
example as a:
• one (1)-year extension;
• two (2)-year extension;
• three (3)-year extension; or
• a combination of increments of one (1) year up to a maximum of three (3) years.
The scope of the Initial Call-off Contract is expected to include (but not be limited to):
• Design and configuration and build of a Property Management System, which includes:
o Integration of current Financial Management System
o Integration of current GIS Mapping System
• Migration of existing data from existing Property Management System
• Ongoing Support and Maintenance (including Support and Platform Updates)
• Training Services
It should be noted that IDA Ireland anticipates that, during the Initial Call-Off Contract, the
anticipated time for the design and implementation of the proposed Property Management System
will be circa. one (1) year.
Further information on the Initial Call-Off Contract will be provided to shortlisted Candidates as part
of this Procurement Process.
3.3.3 Subsequent Call-Off Contracts
Subsequent Call-off Contracts may be awarded pursuant to the Framework Agreement in relation to
the following:
• Additional development projects which may include customisations and integrations.
• Additional capability provided by Salesforce.
• Future support and maintenance of the Salesforce System.
• Additional cloud hosting acquisition / hosting management requirements.
• Ancillary or related services or licenses.
3.3.4 Maximum Value of the Framework Agreement
The maximum total value of any purchases pursuant to the Framework Agreement is €4m (ex. VAT)
(inclusive of any anticipated extensions) over the lifetime of the Framework Agreement. It is
emphasised, however, that this figure is provided strictly for indicative purposes only as there is no
guaranteed expenditure under the Framework Agreement.
3.4 Awarding Call-Off Contracts under the Framework AgreementIDA001/0095-#12514451v2 9
Call-Off Contracts under the Framework Agreement may be awarded directly on foot of the original
tender provided by the Preferred Tenderer or by consultation with the Preferred Tenderer and
invitation to provide a supplementary tender within the constraints laid down in this Procurement
Process and the Framework Agreement’s terms and conditions.
3.5 Use of the Framework Agreement
IDA Ireland intends to use this Framework Agreement as and when requirements within itsscope arise.
However, there is no obligation upon IDA Ireland to make use of this Framework Agreement.
Notwithstanding this fact, the Framework Agreement may be terminated in accordance with its terms
and conditions, a draft of which will be appended to the ITT.
3.6 Award to Runner Up
If for any reason, it is not possible to establish the Framework Agreement or award the Initial CallOff Contract to the designated Preferred Tenderer emerging from this Procurement Process, IDA
Ireland reserves the right to establish the framework with the next highest scoring tenderer on the
basis of the terms advertised at any time during the tender validity period. This shall be without
prejudice to the right of IDA Ireland to cancel this Procurement Process and/or initiate a new contract
award procedure at its sole discretion.
3.7 Competitive Procedure with Negotiation
IDA Ireland is employing the competitive procedure with negotiation as permitted under Regulation
29 of the European Union (Award of Public Authority Contracts) Regulations 2016 (S.I. No. 284 of
2016) (the “2016 Regulations”). IDA Ireland has considered in accordance with Regulation 26 of the
2016 Regulations that the choice of competitive procedure with negotiation is appropriate given the
complexity and risk associated with this Procurement Processin accordance with and the consequent
potential need to seek to negotiate certain elements with Tenderers prior to final submissions. The
procedure involves a number of stages, specified below.
As noted below, there is no requirement on IDA Ireland to enter negotiations with Tenderers and the
Framework Agreement (and Initial Call-off Contract) may be awarded without any negotiations taking
place. Further information will be specified within the Invitation to Tender.
Pre-Qualification Phase (this Phase)
This phase of the Procurement Process (the “Pre-Qualification Phase”) will be used to determine which
Candidates qualify for the Tender Phase of the Procurement Process described below. This
determination will be based on Candidates’ assessed and scored RTP Response Documents. RTP
Response Documents will be evaluated in accordance with the rules set out in the RTP Documentation.
If any specified mandatory criterion is not satisfied or if any specified minimum score is not achieved,
IDA Ireland reserves the right to eliminate the Candidate from the Procurement Process.IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 10
If the RTP Response Document otherwise fails to comply in any respect with the requirements set out
in the RTP Documentation or is ambiguous or if information/documentation is omitted from a RTP
Response Document, IDA Ireland will be entitled at its discretion (but will not be obliged) to take such
steps as it considers appropriate including (but not limited to):
(i) rejecting the relevant RTP Response Document as non-compliant;
(ii) assessing/evaluating the RTP Response Document ‘asis’;
(iii) without prejudice to IDA Ireland’s right to reject the RTP Response Document and in
accordance with Regulation 56(4) of the 2016 Regulations, where it appears to IDA
Ireland that information or documentation submitted by a Candidate is incomplete,
erroneous or missing, IDA Ireland may:
(a) seek clarification from a Candidate in respect of the relevant RTP Response
Document;
(b) request a Candidate to provide IDA Ireland with information or items which
have not been provided or have been provided in an incorrect form or on an
incorrect basis;
(c) request a Candidate to complete any aspect of the relevant RTP Response
Document;
provided however that no clarification or additional information will be sought if, in the opinion of
IDA Ireland, such clarification or additional information would be material.
If those eligible Candidates who meet all pass/fail criteria, achieve all specified minimum scores and
are not otherwise eliminated, the top scoring three (3) Candidates against the selection criteria in
Section B of the RTP Response Document will be selected to proceed to the Tender Phase of the
Procurement Process. IDA Ireland reserves the right to select a fewer number to proceed to the
Tender Phase if there are fewer than three (3) Candidates who submit RTP Response Documents that
meet all pass/fail criteria, achieve all specified minimum scores and are not otherwise eliminated.
Candidates who do not qualify for the Tender Phase of the Procurement Process will be notified in
writing by IDA Ireland.
Tender Phase
Shortlisted Candidates who are selected in the Pre-Qualification Phase (hereinafter referred to as
“Tenderers”) to tender for the Framework Agreement will be invited to participate in the next stage
of the Procurement Process (known as the “Tender Phase”).
Tenderers will be issued with an Invitation to Tender (“ITT”) which will include the following:
(i) minimum specification of requirements to be met by all Tenderers;
(ii) draft Framework Agreement and Initial Call-Off Contract;
(iii) draft Data Processing Agreement;
(iv) further information on the required form and content of Tenders;
(v) further information on structure of the negotiation and Tender Phase;
(vi) further information on tender submission requirements; andIDA001/0095-#12514451v2 11
(vii) details of the award criteria that will be applied as part of the Procurement Process.
Possible award on foot of Initial Tenders, without negotiation
In accordance with Regulation 29(10) of the 2016 Regulations, IDA Ireland reserves the right to
evaluate the initial tenders submitted by shortlisted Candidates in response to the ITT (the “Initial
Tenders”) against the Award Criteria and the evaluation methodology set out in the ITT and to award
the Framework Agreement and Initial Call-Off Contract to the Preferred Tenderer - without further
negotiation.
Optional Negotiations with Tenderers (the “Negotiation Stage”) and Final Tenders
In the event that IDA Ireland opts not to award the Framework Agreement and the Initial Call-off
Contract on the basis of Initial Tenders, it shall instead enter into negotiations with Tenderers in
relation to their Initial Tenders. Tenderers will be invited to attend a negotiation meeting (or meetings)
at which aspects of their Initial Tenders may be discussed.
IDA Ireland reserves the right to negotiate on any aspect of the tender with the exception of the
minimum requirements and the award criteria as stated in the ITT. IDA Ireland reserves the right to
conduct the Negotiation Stage in successive stages in order to reduce the number of tenders to be
negotiated by applying the award criteria. Should IDA Ireland decide to negotiate initial Tenders, it
will provide Tenderers with the details of the process and the timetable in advance of the
negotiations. Further information on any Negotiation Phase of the Procurement Process will be
specified at a later point in the Procurement Process.
Following its determination that such negotiations are concluded, IDA Ireland will set a common
deadline and issue an Invitation to Submit Final Tenders (“ISFT”) to the Tenderers. IDA Ireland reserves
the right to amend and re-issue a further revised draft Framework Agreement and/or Initial Call-Off
Contract with the ISFT; any such further revised form of draft Framework Agreement and/or Initial
Call-Off Contract shall not be subject to additional negotiation as part of the ISFT. Each Tenderer not
eliminated during the Negotiation Stage shall be invited to submit a final tender (“Final Tender”) in
response to the instructions set out in the ISFT.
Final Tenders shall be evaluated in accordance with the Award Criteria and the evaluation
methodology set out in the ITT and ISFT and IDA Ireland reserves the right to award the Framework
Agreement and Initial Call-off Contract to the Preferred Tenderer.
Preferred Tenderer
Whether a Framework Agreement and Initial Call-off Contract is to be awarded on the basis of Initial
Tenders or Final Tenders, IDA Ireland would expect to conclude the Framework Agreement and the
Initial Call-off Contract with the Preferred Tenderer as soon as possible following the standstill period
required by the European Communities (Public Authorities' Contracts) (Review Procedures)
Regulations 2010 (as amended).
The conclusion of any Framework Agreement and any Call-Off Contract (including the Initial Call-Off
Contract) is subject to all necessary approvals being obtained by IDA Ireland, the provision of relevant
documentation by the Preferred Tenderer (e.g., to demonstrate compliance with minimumIDA001/0095-#12514451v2 12
requirements including tax and insurance requirements), the completion of final due diligence (e.g. to
ensure there are no grounds for exclusion), any conditions precedent specified in the ITT/ISFT and all
other legal requirements being satisfied.
Anticipated Timeline
The following indicative timeline is envisaged for this procurement:

Closing Date for Queries September 9th 2026
Closing Date for Submission (Qualification stage) September 25th 2026
Selection Decision October 1st 2026

The dates provided above are estimates at the time of publication of the Invitation to
Participate. IDA Ireland will endeavour to run the process to this timetable, but this cannot
be guaranteed.
3.8 Data Protection and IT Security
Candidates should note that if successfully shortlisted, they will be required to submit evidence of
technical and organisational measures during the Tender Stage to demonstrate compliance with Data
Protection Legislation & IT Security as set out below. This will be incorporated into a Data Processing
Agreement which will be signed by the parties prior to formal commencement of the contract, a copy
of which will be provided at Tender Stage.
1. Information Security Certification
Tenderers must maintain a certified Information Security Management System (ISMS) in accordance
with ISO/IEC 27001 (or equivalent), covering the services and operations relevant to the proposed
Property Management System. .
2. Independent Security Assurance
Tenderers must provide evidence of independent security assurance through ISO/IEC 27001
certification (or equivalent) and a current SOC 2 Type II attestation covering relevant services and
operations.
3. Data Protection & Regulatory Compliance
Tenderers must demonstrate compliance with applicable data protection legislation, including GDPR,
and provide details of their data protection governance arrangements.IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 13
4. Security Incident Management
Tenderers must maintain documented information security incident management processes and be
capable of notifying IDA Ireland of security incidents or personal data breaches affecting the services
provided.
5. Data Hosting & Sub-processors
Tenderers must disclose the geographic locations where customer data will be stored or processed,
including the use of any subcontractors or third-party service providers.
3.8.1 Data Protection Legislation
“Data Protection Laws” means all applicable national and EU data protection laws, regulations and
guidelines including but not limited to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 on the protection of natural persons
with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement ofsuch data, and repealing
Directive 95/46/EC (the “General Data Protection Regulation” or “GDPR”), the Data Protection Act
2018 and any guidelines and codes of practice issued by the Data Protection Commission or other
supervisory authority for data protection in Ireland from time to time. IDA Ireland will be a Controller
(where Controller has the meaning given under the Data Protection Laws) in respect of any Personal
Data (where Personal Data has the meaning given under the Data Protection Laws) required to be
provided by the Candidate in response to this RTP. The Candidate, as Controller in respect of any
Personal Data provided by it in its RTP Response Document, is required to confirm by way of
statement that all Data Subjects (where Data Subject has the meaning given under the Data
Protection Laws) whose Personal Data is provided by the Candidate have consented to the processing
of such Personal Data by the Candidate, IDA Ireland, the Evaluation Team and the supplier of the
etenders.gov.ie website, for the purposes of the participation of the Candidate in this Procurement
Process or that the Candidate otherwise has a legal basis for providing such Personal Data to IDA
Ireland for the purposes of its participation in this Procurement Process.
3.8.2 Transfer of Data outside the European Economic Area (EEA)
It is the intention of IDA Ireland that no data gathered on behalf or entered by IDA Ireland can be
stored or processed outside of the European Economic Area (EEA) for the duration of the contract.
Tenderers need to clearly state where, geographically, the data is stored and processed, backup/DR
data included and confirm that no data is stored or processed outside of the EEA. In the event that
the data needs to be stored and/or processed outside of the EEA, tenderers are asked to specify if an
adequacy decision exists in relation to the non-EU country where they intend data storage and/or
processing to be carried out.
If storage and processing of IDA Ireland’s data is intended to be carried out with the UK, it is the
intention of IDA Ireland to require the inclusion of a Standard Contractual Clause between IDA
Ireland and the Preferred Tenderer in any Call-Off Contract and/or the Framework Agreement.
Tenderers will be required to confirm as part of the Tender Stage that they are willing to engage
with IDA Ireland on putting this measure in place if the situation applies.
For the purposes of the RTP Response Document, Candidates are required to provide the necessary
confirmation in A7 of the RTP Response Document.IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 14
4. Scope of Requirement for the Framework Agreement and the Initial Call-Off Contract
4.1 Context
IDA Ireland’s existing Property Management System (“PMS”) was procured and implemented in 2013
at a time when the scale, value and complexity of the IDA Ireland’s property portfolio and capital
delivery programme were significantly lower than today. The system was designed primarily to support
relatively straightforward sales and lease transactions and to facilitate basic invoice processing, with
limited integration to the broader organisational systems landscape.
Over successive strategy cycles, the Strategic Property Division has experienced a substantial increase
in activity levels, portfolio value, capital investment and operational complexity. This includes
significant growth in land acquisition, major infrastructure projects, advance building delivery,
long-term leasing arrangements, legal case volumes, and the scale of income and expenditure
managed annually. While the existing PMS continues to provide limited transactional tracking, it does
not support the full property lifecycle now required, nor does it integrate with Salesforce, which has
become IDA’s strategic client and operational system of record.
As a result, a significant proportion of core property management activity is conducted outside the
PMS using spreadsheets, email and manual controls. While the Property team continues to operate
very effectively, this fragmented approach presents increasing risks in terms of data quality,
auditability, governance, reporting consistency and operational resilience.
4.1.1 Review of Salesforce Platform Suitability
In 2025, IDA Ireland’s external ICT advisory firm was commissioned to undertake an independent
assessment of whether the Salesforce platform could be leveraged as the foundation for a PMS tailored
to IDA Ireland’s unique requirements. The objective of this engagement was to determine whether an
integrated, Salesforce-based approach could reduce delivery risk, improve long-term value for money,
and avoid introducing another standalone enterprise system into the technology landscape.
The Salesforce suitability assessment and the subsequent high-level design phase is now complete.
The outcome of this work confirms that Salesforce is a viable and stable core platform on which to
deliver a modern PMS for IDA. The agreed solution design indicates the majority of requirements align
to standard capability, with the remaining delivered through controlled configuration and integration.
The high-level design has produced a fully articulated end-to-end solution covering the complete
property lifecycle, including acquisition, property development, finance and lease management, sales
and marketing, legal and conveyancing activities. The high-level design explicitly embeds governance
controls, approval gates, auditability and role-based access throughout the lifecycle, directly
addressing known weaknesses in the current operating environment. Scope is now clearly defined,
technical and data architecture decisions have been made, and delivery assumptions are transparent
and documented. Importantly, the high-level design phase was deliberately separated from any
commitment to build or implement, preserving IDA Ireland’s governance control over cost and delivery
4.1.2 Design Assumptions:
• The PMS will be built on Salesforce, leveraging the client’s existing CRM platform.
• Docusign CLM is the confirmed target platform for controlled PMS document generation,
document storage, versioning and signature workflow. Salesforce remains the process and
metadata layer and exposes access to CLM documents from the relevant PMS records.
• Centros API connection is the confirmed target integration pattern for finance visibility and
outbound invoice/billing requests. Detailed field mapping is treated as a build activity once the
Centros data model and available API entities are provided.
• ArcGIS integration will provide map and boundary visibility in PMS, while spatial/sizing edits
remain managed in ArcGIS. Some Property related data will be synced between PMS and
ArcGIS to avoid duplication of effort.
• The solution will support both IDA-owned assets and selected third-party properties for sales
and marketing use cases.
• Talend will be used as middleware where required to orchestrate and secure integrations
between Salesforce PMS and external systems such as Centros and ArcGIS.
• Property maintenance is confirmed as a lightweight PMS tracking process. The solution will
not implement a heavy Field Service operating model unless a future phase explicitly changes
this scope.
4.1.3 Known Requirements
IDA Ireland’s property assets currently under management comprise c. 1,500ha, c. 150 land banks
nationally together with c. 40 IDA owned building solutions, including those delivered as part of the
IDA Regional Building Programme. The IDA Property team completes between 40-50 sales transactions
per year which generate invoices. There are additional invoices to be generated on building leases &
ground rents on c. 2300 occupational and long leased units. Additionally, there are c. 60-80 licences,
leases, options, wayleaves, rights of way, grazing transactions ongoing with IDA and IDA clients’
solicitors at any one time. The property marketing team also manages over 350 property enquiries
year on year.
IDA Ireland’s success in attracting FDI has often involved clients taking up property stock at scale in
various locations around the country. To continue this and as part of our strategic goal to build clusters
of technical excellence and to maximise regional opportunities, over the next 20 years, we intend to
develop a number of larger scale, pre-permitted Next Generation Sites (“NGS”) at regional locations
that encompass property, utility and sustainable infrastructure that a potential investor can then use
or modify to suit their needs.
Successfully delivering NGS to being investment ready will require commitment to excellent data
management, digitisation & communication. As such, it is expected that there will be a significant
increase in Property activity over the next strategy cycle with a commensurate increase in value &
complexity of transactions together with all the related reporting, information requests & audit
demands.
To this end, IDA Property now requires a PMS that supports its strategic goals through the provision of IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 16
accurate property asset and transaction data together with the ability to consistently generate and
recoup its own resource income from the sale and letting of property assets while managing the overall
risk effectively and efficiently. The proposed PMS must be capable of managing, supporting, and
optimising IDA’s asset base and use technology to fully optimise its property management processes
and record keeping, adopting a digital first approach and seeking to remove/reduce paper as much as
possible.
4.1.4 Expectations from the new PMS – Advantages & Benefits
The required Salesforce-led PMS should offer enhanced security and data integrity with built-in
validation checks, secure access controls, and real-time updates, making it a reliable and incorruptible
solution. An enhanced Salesforce-led Property management information system will also facilitate
sharing of procurement, payment, project management, case management and financial information.
The proposed Salesforce-led PMS will contribute greatly to the modernising and proofing of IDA’s
technology landscape by simplifying and unifying end-to-end processes & ultimately facilitate
improved risk management for Property & client related interactions.
The proposed solution will deliver significant advantages in terms of risk management and compliance
under the following broad areas of work:
• Building Delivery - contract management
• Infrastructure and 3rd Party Contract Management Acquisition - contract management
• Sustainability Tracking and Reporting
• Financial Control and Risk Management
• Conveyance Contracting and Case Management
• Information sharing across Property, Operations and Finance Teams Training and resource
management through task management and tracking functionality
• Management Decision-making, improved metrics, and management reporting Property
Marketing support materials Arc GIS map Viewer where mapping information remain integral
to the new ArcGIS System
Expected Benefits
Strategic Alignment and Organisational Integration: Integration between Property and Operations
will enable the Property team to share and report on richer datasets covering both functions, reducing
duplication and ensuring more consistent client messaging.
Enhanced Financial Integration with Centros (Current IDA Financial Management System):
Integrating property income and expenditure data with the IDA finance system will enable stronger
financial reporting and improve the quality of information available through the property system.
Mitigation of Data Quality Risk: Currently, the proposed integrated system will reduce manual
processes re budget tracking, property marketing activity records, sustainability and green budgeting
data, building and insurance lists, risk registers, and purchase order lists and the associated data quality IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 17
risks.
Enhanced Property Project Management: Information will be available and managed through the
system, facilitating the sharing of procurement, payment, project management, and financial
information. This will support contract cost comparison across teams and improve overall project
management capabilities.
Mapping Integration with ArcGIS: The planned solution with Salesforce will improve the clarity and
accuracy of mapping information, support better decision-making, reduce costly and time-consuming
errors, and increase certainty for both IDA clients and staff.
Enhanced Contact and Case Management capability: The proposed solution will provide a single
source of record for all IDA client and legal interactions, enabling the Property Legal Team to manage
conveyancing cases more efficiently and effectively.
4.1.5 Time scales for Implementation & Ongoing Support
Implementation is intended to commence in early 2027 with an expected duration circa 1 Year. After
hyper care, ongoing support and maintenance would be required for the remainder of the contract.
4.1.6 Expectations of the Provider
The preferred delivery model requires a strategic “partnership”, not a transactional service. The
Preferred Tenderer will be able to demonstrate:
• Proven Track Record / Experience in delivering similar service solutions which are relevant
and comparable with the IDA requirements. As requested by the RTP Response Document,
Candidates should demonstrate a high level of experience, expertise and capability to deliver
the service solution required and should provide examples of how their business activities
relate to the provision of bespoke implementations on the Salesforce platform, referencing
contracts of a similar nature, size, scale and scope to those envisaged by this Procurement
Process.
• Appropriate Team Expertise and Qualifications / Certifications: The Preferred Tenderer will
be required to provide appropriate resourcing levels, of suitably qualified and experienced
personnel, to successfully manage and deliver all the requirements under the Framework
Agreement, including an experienced Helpdesk Team.
• Appreciation of importance of rigorous project and contract management: Accessible
Contract Manager with Programme orchestration skills involving potentially multiple actors
(providers) and delivery streams. Complex project governance, risk management and
performance measurement. Robust internal governance including Steering Committee
participation and structured project management processes. Familiarity with the machinery
of Government and the governance, reporting and commercial implications that flow from
contracting with a public body. IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 18
Candidates should seek to highlight their strengths in these areas in the RTP Response Document as
required by the selection criteria.
4.2 High‑Level Scope of the Framework Agreement
The Framework Agreement covers the full suite of services required to design, deliver, manage, and
evolve a modern property management system that supports the full property lifecycle, improves data
integrity, strengthens governance and reporting, manages transaction cases through caseload
allocations. The system should aim to reduce/eliminate manual dependency on disconnected
spreadsheets, email trails and incumbent-based system workarounds.
The design should capture all Property activities across each sub team including Acquisition, Property
Development, Finance & Lease Management, Sales & Marketing, and Legal & Conveyancing.
IDA Ireland reserves the right, during the lifetime of the Framework Agreement, to draw down
any combination of these services as required, subject to the terms and conditions of the
Framework Agreement. The Framework Agreement does not guarantee any minimum level of
expenditure.
4.3 Scope of the Initial Call-Off Contract
The Initial Call-Off Contract will appoint a partner to design, deliver, and implement a new PMS to
deliver the following target functions & data architecture:
• Property record management across a hierarchical portfolio structure including holdings,
parks, buildings, units and rental spaces.
• Acquisition initiation, approvals, legal handoff, transaction reporting and completion to
portfolio.
• Property development management including project tracking, spend tracking, project phases,
planning, supplier contracts, milestones and capital project reporting.
• Finance and lease management including asset financial activation, lease setup, charge
schedules, lease events, batch invoice request generation and financial visibility.
• Sales and marketing support includes property catalogue search, third-party properties,
transactions, prospect handling, commercial readiness and transaction monitoring.
• Legal and conveyancing support including legal cases, confidentiality controls, advice
generation, mapping/conveyancing tasks and correspondence management.
• Lightweight maintenance tracking for planned and reactive maintenance work, with regional
ownership, FM contractor involvement, purchase order reference and basic reporting.
• Transversal requirements including document generation, email capture, security and access
controls, integrations and reporting.
The target data model is centred on a single property hierarchy and a set of domain-specific
process objects. The following core data model principles are applied:IDA001/0095-#12514451v2 19
• Asset / Property hierarchy is the backbone of the model and supports Holding, Land Bank,
Park, Building, Unit and Rental Space structures.
• Development Projects and KPN (Key Project Numbers) provide capital project traceability
independent of the underlying site hierarchy.
• Lease Agreements are dedicated objects linked to Rental Spaces rather than standard
Contracts with mixed-use record types. There can only be one LIVE / ACTIVE LEASE
AGREEMENT connected to a Rental Space at any time.
• Financial mirrors from Centros are modelled explicitly for reporting and linkage, not for local
accounting control.
